items.title: Alarm files NO finding issue when the job fails before the drift/claims steps run (self-test failure path)
items.note: Found by the 2026-07-25 gate-execution sweep by EXECUTING reverify.yml's `Open finding` body under GitHub's exact shell semantics (`bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail`), not by reading it. When either self-test step fails, `finding.txt` is never created; the step's `cat finding.txt` then exits 1 under `-eo pipefail`, so the step dies BEFORE `gh issue create` and no finding issue is filed. Two consequences: (1) an instrument failure produces a red job but no issue — the drift alarm is silent about its own breakage, which is the same family as the 2026-07-24 never-armed defect; (2) the only diagnostic emitted is `cat: finding.txt: No such file or directory`, which points at the wrong thing. NOT a drift-masking bug: the job still goes red and the workflow-failure notification still fires, so a real drift is never hidden. Severity LOW. Evidence: with finding.txt absent the step exits 1; with a real synthetic drift present it produces title `Drift: constants/21a.md (2026-07-25)`, and with a real BROKEN claim it produces `Drift: claims pin:10a:U (2026-07-25)` — both branches of the title extractor verified FIRING against real tool output.
items.closeWhen: The Open-finding step either files a legibly-titled instrument-failure issue when finding.txt is absent, or a deliberate decision is recorded that a red job alone is sufficient for self-test failures.
items.resolution: FIXED 2026-07-25, same day, David-decided. He chose filing an instrument-failure issue over treating a red job as sufficient — rationale: a red CI run on a once-a-day lane is easy to scroll past, and the failure mode being hidden is our own instrument going quiet, which is precisely what this lane claims to catch. The Open-finding step now branches on `[ -s finding.txt ]`: with check output it behaves exactly as before ('Drift: <what moved>'); without it, it files 'Instrument failure: bounds-ledger self-test (<date>)' with an explicit '(no check output — the job failed before the drift/claims steps ran)' body instead of dying at `cat` and filing nothing. VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, not inspection: the step body was extracted verbatim from the deployed YAML, the `gh issue create` call stripped, and run under GitHub's exact shell (`bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail`) against all three real inputs — absent finding.txt => 'Instrument failure: bounds-ledger self-test (2026-07-25)'; real injected mirror drift => 'Drift: constants/21a.md (2026-07-25)'; real broken pin => 'Drift: claims pin:10a:U (2026-07-25)'. No regression on the two paths that already worked; pipefail guard still passes (step keeps `shell: bash`).
items.note2: SUPERSEDED — read `resolution` above; this fix SHIPPED 2026-07-25 and is live in .github/workflows/reverify.yml (the `[ -s finding.txt ]` branch + the `Instrument failure:` title). Kept only as the pre-fix reasoning. ORIGINAL: READY FIX (deliberately NOT shipped in the sweep — it changes WHEN the alarm files, and the alarm surface is this lane's most load-bearing artifact; 7/24's lesson is that changes here get deliberated): guard the cat and make the title honest, e.g. `cat finding.txt 2>/dev/null || echo '(no check output — job failed before the drift/claims steps ran; see the failed step above)'` plus a title fallback that says instrument-failure rather than `Drift:`. Decide first whether a self-test failure SHOULD file an issue at all — arguably yes, since a steward whose instrument breaks silently is the exact failure mode this lane exists to prevent.

verifyBy.method: re-run the Open-finding body under `bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail` with finding.txt absent and confirm it reaches the issue-create call with a non-misleading title

items.title: Alarm labelled a transient network failure 'Drift:' and omitted the reason entirely (production issue #2)
items.note: CAUGHT IN PRODUCTION 2026-07-25, not by review. CI run 30168372746 (push of 8856fb3, 17:48Z) failed and auto-filed issue #2 titled 'Drift: bounds-ledger re-verification (2026-07-25)' over a body reading '223 claim(s): 222 hold, 0 broken/unreachable' — self-contradictory. No record drifted: reverify.mjs --check hit a transient network error, printed 'error: fetch failed', exited 2; the claims step then ran via if:'!cancelled()' and everything held; the next push ten minutes later was green. TWO DEFECTS. (1) A tool error was titled 'Drift:', asserting a mathematical record moved when none did — the title extraction found no CHANGED/ADDED/REMOVED and no BROKEN/UNREACHABLE lines and fell through to the generic default, which is still prefixed 'Drift:'. (2) The reason was invisible: reverify.mjs reports errors via console.error (stderr) but the step piped only stdout (`| tee`), so 'error: fetch failed' reached the CI log and never the issue body. Same failure family as the 2026-07-24 never-armed defect from the opposite direction — that alarm could not speak, this one spoke and said the wrong thing. Cost model: a false 'Drift:' burns a reader's time hunting a record change that never happened, and repeated flakes train us to skim past Drift: issues, which is how a REAL drift gets missed. Finding: docs/findings/2026-07-25-alarm-called-a-network-flake-a-drift.md.
items.closeWhen: A tool/network error produces an honestly-titled issue that states the cause, and a real drift still titles as a drift.
items.resolution: FIXED 2026-07-25 same day. (a) `2>&1` added to both piped check steps so stderr lands in finding.txt and therefore in the issue body; (b) the title now branches three ways instead of falling through — 'Drift: <what moved>' on real drift/claim lines, 'Check error: … could not complete' when finding.txt contains an ^error: line, 'Re-verification failed' otherwise (A-4 supplies a fourth, 'Instrument failure', when finding.txt does not exist at all). VERIFIED BY EXECUTION under GitHub's exact shell (bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail) against four real inputs including a byte-accurate replay of run 30168372746: replay => 'Check error: bounds-ledger re-verification could not complete (2026-07-25)'; absent finding.txt => 'Instrument failure: bounds-ledger self-test (2026-07-25)'; injected mirror drift => 'Drift: constants/21a.md (2026-07-25)'; broken pin => 'Drift: claims pin:10a:U (2026-07-25)'. npm test green; all 5 piped workflow steps still carry shell: bash.
items.note2: RESOLVES TWO SWEEP UNKNOWNS, for free and within the hour. The 2026-07-25 gate-execution sweep marked the composite CI failure path (if: failure() -> gh issue create) and if:'!cancelled()' on the claims step as UNKNOWN, because closing them would have required pushing a corrupted mirror. Production answered both: the issue-filing path FIRES (issue #2 exists) and !cancelled() FIRES (claim output appears in the body although the mirror step had already failed) — and the output was WRONG, which a green could never have revealed. Method lesson worth keeping: the honest UNKNOWN left the question open, so the evidence was recognised when it arrived; a fabricated green would have closed it and issue #2 would have been read as a real drift.
items.note3: DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT: retry/backoff on a transient fetch failure. One flake in four days does not justify it, and suppressing the alarm is the wrong direction. If check-error issues become frequent, add retry inside reverify.mjs — never silence the step.

verifyBy.method: replay the deployed Open-finding body under `bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail` against a finding.txt containing an ^error: line and confirm the title says Check error, not Drift

items.note2: WHY THIS MATTERS FOR G-1, which is the real point. G-1 needs at least one EXTERNALLY-ACKNOWLEDGED correction and that metric is currently 0, resting entirely on one email to one busy maintainer who owes us nothing. Two independent improvements are now available: (1) SCALE THE CATCHES — erdosproblems.com is the most-used index in the field and we already know it goes stale (that is the lane founding finding). Systematically diffing its bounds against Tao curated table across many problems turns one lucky catch into a repeatable pipeline of correction candidates. (2) CHANGE THE CHANNEL — a PR against a community database with a CONTRIBUTING.md is mechanically reviewable and leaves a public, dated, attributable record. An accepted PR IS an external acknowledgement, and unlike an email it cannot be silently ignored into ambiguity. Email put the north-star metric behind an inbox; a PR puts it behind a merge button.
items.note3: SEQUENCING / CAUTION. Real feature build, not cleanup — do not start it inside a close-out. EVIDENCE IS gh api OUTPUT, per the ruling, not a settings page. R16: repository ruleset `main-history-integrity` id 20607202, `enforcement: active`, `bypass_actors: []`, `current_user_can_bypass: never`, rules `[deletion, non_fast_forward]`, include `[~DEFAULT_BRANCH]`. No required-review rule and that is deliberate: single contributor, so requiring PRs adds friction without adding a reviewer. A future deliberate history rewrite must now disable the ruleset first — intended friction on an irreversible action, and worth knowing before someone reads a rejected push as a broken remote. R5: `git config core.hooksPath` → `.githooks`; the hook runs `history-sweep.mjs --staged`, a NEW MODE OVER THE SAME PATTERN SET rather than a second scanner — two secret matchers drift apart and the one nobody watches is the one that goes quiet. R4: repo-health.json at root (4967 bytes, readable via the contents API), written for a PUBLIC reader — it states the controls that are in place and names gaps by tracker ID only, deliberately publishing no weakness inventory, because doing exactly that was one of the eight blockers of the 2026-08-05 pre-publication review. DEMONSTRATED BOTH WAYS at the real boundary, not just against the function: ordinary prose staged → CLEAN exit 0; a planted ghp_ token staged → `git commit` REFUSED exit 1 with nothing landing; and our own real commit of this work printed CLEAN as it went through. The ruleset's silent half is demonstrated too — the push of 0a29081 was a fast-forward and succeeded.
items.note6: ONE DEMONSTRATION IS OWED ON R16, and it is not being quietly skipped. Proving the ruleset FIRES requires attempting a real force-push, and the Claude Code auto-mode classifier REFUSED that command. Per the 2026-08-08 standing rule I did not substitute a smaller equivalent operation (a rewind push, a rebase, an amend) to get around the refusal — that defeats the gate's intent, and the hand-off is a ~2-minute detour. So the state read stands as evidence that the rule is CONFIGURED AND ACTIVE and is NOT evidence that it fires, exactly the distinction drawn for secret scanning and push protection on 8/08. THE OWED DEMONSTRATION, one command, safe and recoverable: `git push --force origin HEAD~1:main` — expected to be REJECTED with a ruleset violation; if it somehow succeeded, main rewinds one commit and `git push origin main` restores it in seconds. David can run it with the in-session `! <command>` form. DELIBERATELY NOT ATTEMPTED, and this is a scoping judgment rather than an oversight: the `deletion` rule was not separately exercised, because the failure mode of an unenforced test is deleting main on a public repo, and a probe licenses its own claim and nothing wider (the 8/04 F-4 lesson) — so do NOT read a demonstrated non-fast-forward rejection as proof the deletion rule fires.
items.redProofWaived: R16 FIRE DEMONSTRATION WAIVED 2026-08-09 by orchestrator ruling, with reason recorded rather than the requirement quietly dropped. GROUNDS: the rule-suite records are WITHIN-PATH evidence, a rung above a config read — suites 3612293601 and 3612300581 (both `result: pass`, refs/heads/main) show GitHub's enforcement engine adjudicating every push to main, so the rule is demonstrably in the push path and not merely present in settings. Producing a REJECTION would require attempting exactly the operation the ruleset exists to prevent; the Claude Code classifier refuses it, and the ruling explicitly endorsed the refusal to substitute a smaller equivalent operation. DIRECTED NOT TO HAND THIS TO DAVID — the `! git push --force origin HEAD~1:main` ask named in note6 is WITHDRAWN; do not re-raise it with him. WHAT THIS WAIVER DOES AND DOES NOT SAY, because a waiver that blurs into a demonstration is worse than an open gap: it accepts within-path evaluation as sufficient for THIS control, on THIS repo, where the fire test is itself the hazard. It does not establish that a control may be recorded as demonstrated on a state read, and it does not extend to the `deletion` rule (never exercised) or to secret scanning / push protection (enabled 8/08, still never seen to fire, still excluded from closeWhen by design). If the enforcement path is ever seen to reject a push, capture the `result: fail` suite row — GitHub's record outlives our transcript.

items.onTrigger:
When you are about to ship anything whose job is to DETECT (test, guard, lint, probe, --check mode, alarm), before committing: (1) construct the condition it exists to catch and confirm it FIRES, naming what it printed; (2) restore and confirm it goes SILENT; (3) prove the mutation actually landed with git diff --numstat BEFORE believing either result -- a control written with 
 against these CRLF files silently no-ops and manufactures a false inert verdict (2026-07-25); (4) paste both outputs into the commit message or finding doc. If nothing in the repo currently trips it, build a fixture that does -- a detector validated only against a clean world tells you nothing. Then ask the second question, which is NOT the same: can it see the SHAPE of failure that matters, or only one direction of it? (2026-07-31: both detectors passed can-it-fire and both were blind to a class this lane exists to catch.) Finally: is it wired into something that RUNS on its own? A check only in npm scripts is not a detector.

items.noteInstrument: SAMPLER STOOD UP 2026-08-09, which is what this watch's onTrigger asked for and nobody had built: the traffic API retains 14 days, so the 90-day visitor count cannot be reconstructed later — it has to be accumulated. `scripts/traffic-snapshot.mjs` (npm run traffic) merges the daily views/clones window into continuity/traffic.json and prints days-since-flip plus the running totals. It renders NO verdict; the fair-read judgment stays with whoever adjudicates this watch, same reason a generated pin asserts listing position and never 'the record'. Auth is delegated to the `gh` CLI, so no traffic credential enters this now-public repo and the sampler deliberately does NOT run in CI; only its merge is guarded there (10th self-test), because a merge that returned just the incoming window would silently destroy every day older than 14 — the one bug that would eat the record we are building. Both sides demonstrated at write time per W-4/KP-78: with the truncating merge in place the self-test exits 1 naming the dropped history, with it restored exit 0. FIRST SAMPLE, and it needs reading carefully rather than celebrating: 14 days recorded, 1 unique viewer-day since the flip, 25 unique cloner-days. THE CLONE FIGURE IS NOT ARRIVALS — 74 clones / 25 uniques all landed on 8/08, the day we ourselves cloned the remote repeatedly to verify the history rewrite, plus CI checkouts and whatever crawls a repo the minute it goes public. Views are the honest metric and they read 1. MEASUREMENT LIMIT FOUND, and it changes how this watch must be read: GitHub dedupes uniques only WITHIN a 14-day window, so a 90-day figure can only be a SUM of per-day uniques, which counts a returning visitor once per day. That sum is an UPPER BOUND on distinct people — which is the useful direction here: a sum under 100 conclusively settles that the threshold is NOT met, while a sum over 100 does not settle that it is. The closeWhen's '100 unique visitors' is therefore not directly measurable and must be read as 'upper bound at least 100, then look harder'.
items.note2: WHAT WOULD FALSIFY IT / make me revert or replace it: an issue arriving that is NOT about the ledger's correctness (support questions, feature requests, spam) at a rate that makes the channel noise rather than signal; or a real correction arriving by some OTHER route (a PR, an upstream comment, an email) while the issue tracker stays empty — which would say the invitation is in the wrong place, not that nobody wanted to speak. items.title: MIRROR BLIND CLASS: README.md is not mirrored, and it is where upstream states which records it stands behind
items.note: Found inside the 2026-08-02 fourth-drift cycle (A-2 note6). We mirror constants/** + manifest.json (111 files); upstream README.md is NOT in the mirror. Commit dee1660 -- 'Mark C_21 and C_71 unverified records with asterisks in README' -- restored the peer-reviewed OT2013 value as the headline anchor for C_71 and marked the Numaro n=18 record (merged minutes earlier, PR #130) as unverified because it is on Zenodo but not yet peer-reviewed. Our drift alarm reported three constants files and was SILENT on the semantically largest change of the day. WHY IT IS LOAD-BEARING, not academic: generated pins assert listing position inside the per-constant tables, while README is where upstream declares which of those rows it will STAND BEHIND. A record demoted from headline to asterisked is a real event -- arguably the most decision-relevant kind for anyone citing these numbers -- and we cannot see it. Same shape as BC-2 (A-11): the instrument is blind to the class the lane most exists to catch. SEPARATE FROM A-11, which is about check-claims' presence-test on OFF-mirror sources; this one is about the SCOPE of the mirror itself.
items.closeWhen: Either UPSTREAM's README.md (teorth/optimizationproblems' generated 421KB index — NOT this repo's own README.md) joins the mirrored surface with the drift alarm demonstrated firing on an asterisk/headline change and silent on an unrelated edit (W-4), OR a deliberate decision is recorded that the verified/unverified distinction is out of scope for this ledger, with the reason.
items.onTrigger: Before adopting: check how often README churns. It is a GENERATED table (the 8/01 research noted it is the repo's rendered index, 421KB), so a whole-file byte mirror may be as permanently-red as teorth/erdosproblems' problems.yaml was -- which is exactly why A-6 chose entry-level pins over a mirror there. The likely right shape is the A-6 shape: pin the specific README cells for constants we already track, not the file. Decide that before writing code.

verifyBy.method: demonstrate both sides per W-4 -- an asterisk/headline change on a tracked constant must fire, an unrelated README edit must not

items.resolution: CLOSED 2026-08-10 by the first branch of its own closeWhen: upstream README.md joined the mirrored surface, with the drift alarm demonstrated BOTH ways. Greenlit off the capacity ask (David's fire-don't-wait blanket) as the lane's #1 candidate. WHAT SHIPPED: file maps are now keyed by REPO-RELATIVE path (constants/1a.md, README.md) instead of bare filename, so a report names files as upstream does -- the old code prefixed 'constants/' by concatenation and would have printed 'constants/README.md', a lie about where the file lives inside an artifact whose whole value is being literally true. Nothing moved on disk: the 111 constants files stayed put, README sits beside them at the mirror root, and git diff --numstat after the re-snapshot showed ZERO content lines changed in any constants file (manifest + two scripts + one new file). Post-snapshot ratchet ran: extract-pins regenerated BYTE-IDENTICAL (220 generated + 9 hand), independently confirming no bounds-table row moved. Mirror 111 -> 112 files @ dee1660; ledger unchanged at 229 claims / 227 hold / 0 broken / 2 unverified. BOTH ANSWERS DEMONSTRATED, wired into reverify.test.mjs so it is guarded on every CI run: FIRES -- append an asterisk to a real README table row in upstream's own convention, check exits 1 reporting CHANGED README.md with the row verbatim; SILENT (restored) -- put it back and the same run exits 0; SILENT (unrelated edit) -- tamper a constants file and the verdict list is EXACTLY 'CHANGED constants/<file>', README not dragged in (without this, a mirror reporting every file on every run would pass the FIRES assertion while carrying no information); REMOVED -- delete the mirrored README and it reports REMOVED rather than passing silently. NEGATIVE CONTROL PERFORMED with the mutation proven to land first (files are CRLF): ROOT_FILES=[] gives 'AssertionError: an asterisked README row should exit 1, got 0' -- the alarm goes silent on exactly the event class it was built for; restoring returns PASS. THE ITEM OVERSTATED ITS OWN COST BY ~17x AND THAT IS THE TRANSFERABLE PART: closeWhen described a 'generated 421KB index'; the file is 24KB. The 421KB figure belongs to a DIFFERENT repo's README (teorth/erdosproblems, from A-6 scoping) and was copied across at write time. That wrong number is a plausible reason the item sat eight days -- 421KB of near-daily churn reads like a permanently-red alarm waiting to happen, which this lane refuses to ship; 24KB of curated table does not. The estimate, not the value, kept it parked. The check that would have caught it costs one curl: an item's description of its own cost is a claim like any other, and this repo does not accept unexecuted claims from anyone, including itself. ONE ASSERTION WAS WRONG FIRST TIME AND THE ALARM WAS RIGHT: the unrelated-edit check originally asserted the string 'README.md' was absent from the report and failed immediately, because the report HEADER names the whole watched surface. Body was correct throughout. Fixed by asserting on verdict lines rather than raw text, which is also stricter -- it now pins the exact SET of files named. SCOPE HONESTY: this watches upstream's DECLARATION about its records, not the mathematics; a byte-mirror fires on any README edit including a typo fix, accepted deliberately because the file is small and the alternative (pinning only table spans) would reintroduce a blind class to avoid a minor annoyance. Finding: docs/findings/2026-08-10-w5-the-readme-is-where-upstream-says-what-it-stands-behind.md.

items.title: GOAL: contribute a verified bound improvement to the stewarded inventory (steward → steward + contributor; David-ruled 2026-08-06)
items.note: DAVID'S RULING, 2026-08-06, in-session after reading OpenAI's Ten Advances paper: that this was the kind of work he wanted this lane doing — then, on the four-step plan (gap table → pick 2-3 under-studied targets → LLM-proposes / local-verifier-scores search loop → exact reverify + literature check + adversarial review + David-gated PR): to do all four steps. SCOPE HONESTY, recorded at write time: we play the CONSTRUCTION game (an explicit object plus a finite certificate a script can check), never the theorem game (asymptotic proofs need mathematicians or Lean, which we do not have). The certificate IS the contribution — a claim ships only with a verifier the maintainer can run. GUARD: the late-2025 'solved 10 Erdos problems' embarrassment (a model rediscovering known results) is the named failure mode; the literature/priority check is a mandatory step, not hygiene. STEP 1 DONE same day: scripts/gap-table.mjs (selftest wired into npm test + CI) — 111 constants, 65 with a numeric gap, 6 parse-suspect (instrument flags, listed in docs/gap-table.json), 40 symbolic. TARGETS PICKED from reading the files, not the ranks alone: PRIMARY 27b (Earth-Moon problem, max chromatic number of biplanar graphs, bounds 9..12, lower bound unmoved since Sulanke 1980, Gethner conjectures 11; an improvement is a graph + a two-planar edge partition + a DRAT unsatisfiability certificate for (k-1)-coloring — every link machine-checkable); SECONDARY 69a (Sendov radius — lower-bound examples are explicit polynomials, checkable with interval arithmetic); STRETCH 39a (Hadwiger H_3, upper 14 Prymak 2023 — computer-assisted covering method, but the discretization reduction is proof-shaped so a win needs a mathematician-grade gate, riskier); REJECTED 73a after reading (its lower bound is the conjectured optimum — nothing to improve; the gap-table rank alone would have wasted a campaign on it, which is why target-picking reads files). BUDGET, David-asked, answered same session: per-target campaign hard-capped; numbers in the 2026-08-06 daily/bus post.

David greenlit the first campaign in-pane (to go ahead and attempt one, and not to economise on model selection) and ruled Fable drives the proposal step — his instinct endorsed with one refinement recorded here: proposals AND strategy/diagnosis calls get the top model; the VERIFIER gets no model at all, its authority is being dumb checkable code the maintainer can run. Shipped: search/27b/verifier.mjs (exact DMP planarity + exact branch-and-bound chromatic number + certificate check, Node stdlib only), selftest proving both answers (4 nonplanar fire incl. Petersen and K3,3 which exercise the real embedding not the edge count; 4 planar silent; 5 exact chi values; 1 good certificate passes, 3 defect classes fail), wired into npm test + CI. Then the known-record reproduction: a random-restart greedy (deterministic PRNG, seed recorded) found a biplanar split of Sulanke's graph on restart 924 - 27/23 edges, both layers planar under DMP, chi exactly 9 - and the full certificate verifies: search/27b/sulanke-certificate.json. The harness can score the known answer; searching for a 10-chromatic biplanar graph may now begin. SEARCH POSTURE: Fable proposes construction families in-session (subscription, ~zero marginal cost) with the verifier as the only judge; API-billed overnight runs come later if volume demands, and need an API key decision from David first. CEILING RECORDED AT WRITE TIME: the in-house chromatic solver is exponential worst-case and fine at n<=40; a real candidate for upstream gets a DIMACS export + industrial SAT solver + DRAT proof as the shipping certificate, not our solver's word.
items.note3: ROUND ONE RAN 2026-08-07: 11 proposed constructions, 0 certified, 11 eliminated (edge-bound 5, k9-free 2, chromatic 4). Instrument: search/27b/propose-round.mjs, 8th self-test, wired into npm test + CI and proven both ways (each of 4 gates fires and stays silent; split search returns both outcomes; Sulanke re-certifies at target 9; and the CI wiring itself was negative-controlled — removing the workflow step made reverify.test exit 1 naming the unguarded selftest, restoring it returned exit 0 / 8 self-tests). FINDING (docs/findings/2026-08-07-g2-27b-round-one-the-one-edge-vise.md): two unrelated families land EXACTLY one short. The join family successor C5+K7 is over the 6n-12 budget by exactly ONE edge and has omega=9; buying that edge back from inside the clique meets budget exactly and drops omega to 8 but gives chi=9, buying it back from the join keeps omega=9 and dies on the clique gate. Independently, circulants sized to fit the budget top out at C17(1..5) with chi=9. Both directions arrive at nine. The vise: thickness 2 caps average degree below 12 so a 10-chromatic biplanar graph sits near the Brooks boundary where structure is pushed toward near-complete, while thickness 2 simultaneously forbids K9. ROUND TWO DIRECTION, falling straight out of the data (every death was too-dense-to-be-biplanar or not-chromatic-enough, none subtle): INVERT THE SEARCH — stop proposing high-chromatic graphs and hoping they are biplanar; glue two planar triangulations on a shared vertex set so biplanarity is free by construction, and maximise chi, the one gate we compute exactly and cheaply. PROVENANCE: the k9-free gate is CITED (theta(K9)=3, Battle-Harary-Kodama 1962), not executed — 2^36 splits is not brute-forceable and greedy failure proves nothing; labelled CITED in code, console and JSON. Its failure direction is safe: a wrong citation can only make us SKIP a family, never SHIP a false certificate. METHOD CATCH: the first run built two differently-labelled candidates as the SAME graph (positional edge-drop hit cross edges in a join, so the clique-edge candidate was never built); caught only by noticing two rows that should differ did not, NOT by the self-test, which tests the gates and not the candidate list pointed at them (A-13 F-4 shape). Fixed with removeEdge(g,u,v) which throws on a named edge that is not present; the correction changed the result and exposed the chi=9 near-miss the finding rests on. NO MATHEMATICAL CLAIM: 0 certificates, and the chi=9 outputs merely re-derive the 1980 bound.
items.note4: ROUND TWO RAN 2026-08-07 (same day as round one): the INVERTED search — build biplanar graphs BY CONSTRUCTION (double-greedy two maximal planar layers out of K_n using the exact DMP test, union is thickness<=2 by construction) and measure chi. Instrument search/27b/round2-grow.mjs, 9th self-test, wired into npm test + CI. RESULT: hard ceiling at chi=8 across n=9..13, 300 seeds each — the inverted search tops out ONE COLOUR BELOW the record it was meant to beat, and degrades as n grows (n=9: 286/300 seeds reach 8; n=13: only 54/300, leftover grows 1->15). THE SENTENCE WORTH KEEPING: at n=11 the best round-two graph has EXACTLY 50 edges and chi=8, while Sulanke has n=11, EXACTLY 50 edges and chi=9 — same vertex count, same edge count, one colour apart, both verified by the same code in the same run. DENSITY IS NOT WHAT THE RECORD IS MADE OF; the objective behind the inverted search is measurably wrong, and this is the cleanest refutation of it. What separates them is STRUCTURE: Sulanke is a designed object (6-clique joined to a 5-cycle) and double-greedy explores the generic part of the space where that never arises by chance. SIDE RESULT, carefully bounded: at n=9 the grower produced K9 minus exactly one edge with both layers planar per the verifier — an EXECUTED demonstration that K9-minus-an-edge is biplanar (chi=8). That is CONSISTENT WITH the theta(K9)=3 citation the round-one k9-free gate leans on, but is NOT a proof of it and must never be recorded as one: exhibiting a split for K9-e says nothing about non-existence of a split for K9. The citation stays cited. ROUND THREE DIRECTION (both rounds now agree from opposite directions that the record is a STRUCTURED object — round one showed structured constructions fail by razor-thin margins, round two shows unstructured ones do not get close): seed the growth with structure. Next instrument should accept a SEED SUBGRAPH held fixed in the layers and double-greedy only the remaining edges; watch the leftover column, which at n>=12 is already large enough to be where the missing colour goes. METHOD CATCH: cross-checking the n=11 comparison by importing round2-grow.mjs silently re-ran the whole search and printed a second full result table into the middle of the check — harmless only because the numbers agreed. Both round scripts exported functions AND ran main at import; both now guard on being the entry point, proven both ways (import prints nothing and still exposes growBiplanar/runGates; direct invocation still runs). NO MATHEMATICAL CLAIM: 0 certificates at target, best chi found is 8, the record lower bound of 9 stands untouched and round two did not even reach it.
items.note5: ROUND THREE RAN 2026-08-10: seed the search with the design, as round two's finding directed. Instrument search/27b/round3-seeded.mjs, 11th self-test, wired into npm test + CI. TWO HALVES, AND THE CHEAP ONE WAS DECISIVE. PART A — THE FAMILY IS CLOSED BY EDGE COUNT ALONE: Sulanke's graph is K6 join C5 and that family has chi = r+3, so chi>=10 needs r>=7; every biplanar graph obeys m <= 6n-12 (two planar layers of 3n-6). Scanning K_r join C_s for r=4..9, odd s=3..11 (30 members): 15 reach chi>=10, and exactly ONE of those fits the budget. Near misses are as thin as round one's — K7 join C5 is over by exactly ONE edge (n=12, m=61, budget 60), K8 join C3 also by exactly one (n=11, m=55, budget 54); every other chi>=10 member misses by 5 to 38. THE SOLE SURVIVOR IS K7 join C3, WHICH IS K10 — verified by execution, not inspection: the construction returns n=10, m=45, and C(10,2)=45, so the graph is complete; its chi was COMPUTED as 10, not taken from the r+3 formula. K10 has thickness 3 (Battle-Harary-Kodama 1962; the theta(K_n) formula's only exceptions are n=9 and n=10), so it is not biplanar and the family is closed. WHERE THIS RESTS ON A CITATION, STATED PLAINLY: the budget half is ours and runs; the theta(K10)=3 step is CITED, not executed — our verifier can exhibit a split when one exists but cannot prove none does, and non-existence is exactly what that step needs. Same citation round one leaned on for K9, same status. PART B — THE SEED CARRIES ALL THE COLOUR AND THE GREEDY CARRIES NONE: holding Sulanke's verified layers fixed and double-greedying only the edges the seed does not own, over n=11..14 at 40 seeds each (160 growths, every graph re-checked by verifyCertificate), best chi is 9 at EVERY n and on EVERY seed — 40/40, never below, never above. Read against round two (which reached 8 on 209/300 seeds at n=10 and only 54/300 by n=13), this is sharp in both directions: the structure survives generic growth, and generic growth adds nothing on top of it. It was still possible after round two that unseeded search underperformed merely because it never stumbled onto the structure; handed the structure outright, it still adds no colour. Leftover behaves as round two predicted: 5 -> 9 -> 14 -> 21 as n grows, i.e. the price of biplanarity rises faster than extra vertices can pay for it. WHAT THIS CLOSES: the clique-join-odd-cycle family as a route to chi=10, and the extend-the-record-graph-generically idea — both live hypotheses that morning, neither needing another search. ROUND FOUR DIRECTION, falling out of the budget scan: every construction tried so far is a JOIN, and a join buys three colours for r*s edges while the 6n-12 budget grows by only 6 per vertex — the next family must buy colour more cheaply per edge than a complete join does. NO MATHEMATICAL CLAIM: 0 certificates at target, best chi found is 9 — equal to the record and only because we handed the search the record graph — and the record lower bound stands untouched. Finding: docs/findings/2026-08-10-g2-27b-round-three-the-family-is-closed.md.
